blocks.x: Just 1 Week Later, Tom Cruise’s Ambitious New Movie Is Officially Getting the IMAX Boot

blocks.c: Tom Cruise and Riz Ahmed in 'Digger'
Tom Cruise and Riz Ahmed in 'Digger'

blocks.x: The IMAX Corporation has confirmed that Christopher Nolan's record-breaking blockbuster, The Odyssey, will return to premium large-format venues as early as this week, following the box-office failure of Digger. Starring Tom Cruise and directed by the two-time Oscar-winning Alejandro G. Iñárritu, the epic sci-fi political satire made less than $20 million worldwide in its box-office debut, against a budget that has been reported to be anywhere between $140 million and $180 million. Warner Bros. spent an additional $100 million to market the movie, meaning that its break-even point, given the typical revenue split between studios and exhibitors, should be around $350 million worldwide. At this rate, Digger is poised to gross around $50 million in its lifetime run.

Also featuring Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Michael Stuhlbarg, and Sandra Hüller, the movie opened to divisive reviews, with some hailing it as a masterpiece while others dismissed its attempts at satire. The movie is sitting at a 51% score on the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, where the consensus reads, "A stylized satire whose audacious design proves too mannered for some of the laughs to smoothly land, Digger is a bold swing of the shovel by Tom Cruise and Alejandro González Iñárritu that misses as often as it strikes gold." In her review, Collider's Victoria Luxford described it as "a film that thrives on defying expectations," and "Cruise’s best work in years."

Which Criminal Mastermind Would Be Your Nemesis?
Lecter · Joker · Moriarty · Chigurh

Four of the finest criminal minds ever put on screen. One of them would look at you and see something worth their time. Eight questions decide which one comes for you, why they picked you, and what they would want when they arrived.

What would a criminal mastermind notice about you first?
Great villains choose their opponents carefully. Something about you got their attention.

AMy manners, and everything I am careful not to say.
BThat I still believe people are basically decent.
CThat I am clever, and quietly enjoy proving it.
DThat I handle things myself, and always have.

How do they make first contact?
The introduction tells you everything about what is coming next.

AA polite letter. Beautiful handwriting. Quietly wrong.
BSomething on fire, with a message left beside it.
CA puzzle, left where only I would look.
DNo contact. Just the aftermath, and a coin.

What do you actually believe about right and wrong?
Every nemesis is really an argument about the thing you believe most.

AThere are lines. Mine are private and absolute.
BRules are the only thing keeping us from being animals.
CMorality is a system, and systems can be solved.
DThings happen. Most of it was never up to me.

What finally gets under your skin?
Everybody has a pressure point. Finding yours is the whole plan.

ABeing seen clearly by somebody I cannot read.
BWatching good people do something ugly.
CLosing to someone who was simply better prepared.
DHaving no move left that changes anything.

They have made their move. How do you fight back?
This is the part of the film where the audience finds out who you are.

ACarefully, and never where they expect to be touched.
BLoudly. I would rather lose than play their game.
CWith a better plan. I can out-think this.
DDirectly, once, with whatever is closest to hand.

What would they use against you?
A good villain never brings a weapon you have not already handed them.

AMy privacy. I have kept far too much to myself.
BMy conscience. I will not cross the line they want.
CMy ego. I cannot resist a worthy opponent.
DMy certainty that I can handle it alone.

What do they actually want from you?
The money is never the point. Something else always is.

ATo understand me better than anyone ever has.
BTo prove I am no better than they are.
CTo finally be beaten by someone worth the trouble.
DNothing at all. I stepped into the wrong path.

How does it end between the two of you?
Eight questions in, this is the one that decides who comes for you.

AA conversation I will be replaying for years.
BA choice forced on me that has no clean answer.
COne final move, and the better mind wins.
DA coin in the air, and nothing I can say.

blocks.x: While Digger's initial release concluded The Odyssey's IMAX run after nearly 80 days, Nolan's fantasy epic will return to both digital IMAX and IMAX 70mm venues this week. The movie holds the record for the biggest-ever IMAX gross, which is currently sitting at more than $500 million worldwide. Overall, The Odyssey has grossed more than $620 million domestically and around $1.76 billion worldwide. It received widespread acclaim upon release, and is now sitting at a "Certified Fresh" 94% score on Rotten Tomatoes. Starring Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, and Robert Pattinson, The Odyssey emerged as Nolan's highest-grossing hit, and is poised to pass the $1.8 billion mark worldwide thanks to a return to IMAX this week. It's also a hot favorite in a dozen categories at the Oscars, while Digger will have to claw its way back into awards-season conversation following its divisive reception. Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.
